source.method: chapter titles from each book's Contents page (First Flight's poems, listed on its Contents page under the units, are chapters of their own); topics from each chapter PDF's own units: the text, Thinking about the Text/Poem, each titled language exercise, and the speaking, listening and writing tasks

topics.title: Reading the Story
objectives: Student can narrate how a hailstorm destroyed Lencho's corn field and why he wrote a letter to God
Student can explain how the postmaster and the post office employees responded to the letter
Student can explain why Lencho was angry when he counted the money
visualIdeas: a lone house on a hill with hailstones falling on the corn field
a letter addressed "To God" on the postmaster's desk

topics.title: Thinking about the Text
objectives: Student can explain Lencho's complete faith in God with sentences from the story
Student can explain the irony of Lencho calling the post office employees crooks
Student can describe the two kinds of conflict in the story: humans and nature, and humans and humans
visualIdeas: a two-column chart: what Lencho expects and what really happened

topics.title: Thinking about Language: Words for Storms and the Word Hope
objectives: Student can match storm words such as gale, whirlwind, cyclone, hurricane, tornado and typhoon to their descriptions
Student can distinguish uses of hope as a verb and as a noun and match expressions with hope to their meanings
visualIdeas: six storm types drawn as small weather icons

topics.title: Relative Clauses
objectives: Student can identify non-defining relative clauses that begin with who, whom, whose or which
Student can join two sentences using a relative pronoun with correct commas
Student can recognise a relative clause in which the relative pronoun is hidden
visualIdeas: a sentence with the relative clause highlighted between commas

topics.title: Using Negatives for Emphasis
objectives: Student can distinguish negative words that show absence from negative words used for emphasis
Student can find sentences in the story where negatives emphasise an idea
visualIdeas: a sentence card: "The hail has left nothing"

topics.title: Metaphors
objectives: Student can explain a metaphor as transferring a quality of one thing to another
Student can identify metaphors in the story, such as huge mountains of clouds, and the quality compared
visualIdeas: clouds drawn as mountains next to the sentence

topics.title: Speaking and Listening
objectives: Student can speak about a time of great difficulty and how the problem was solved
Student can listen to a letter and complete a table about who wrote it, to whom and why
Student can design a poster on saving water during summer and in times of excess
visualIdeas: a poster on rainwater harvesting

topics.title: Reading and Thinking about the Poem
objectives: Student can explain how a crow shaking down a dust of snow from a hemlock tree changed the poet's mood
Student can explain what the crow and the hemlock usually stand for and why Frost chose them
Student can explain how a small moment can have a larger significance
visualIdeas: a crow on a snowy hemlock branch with snow falling on a person below

topics.title: Reading and Thinking about the Poem
objectives: Student can explain the two ideas of how the world may end that the poem presents
Student can explain what fire (desire) and ice (hate) stand for in the poem
Student can identify the rhyme scheme and how it brings out the contrast
visualIdeas: a globe half in flames and half frozen

chapters.title: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom

topics.title: Reading the Text
objectives: Student can describe the inauguration of South Africa's first democratic, non-racial government on 10 May
Student can explain apartheid and Mandela's idea that the depths of oppression created heights of character
Student can explain the twin obligations Mandela speaks of and how his idea of freedom changed with age
visualIdeas: the Union Buildings in Pretoria with a crowd and jets in the sky
a timeline of Mandela's idea of freedom from boy to man

topics.title: Thinking about the Text
objectives: Student can explain why many international leaders attended the inauguration and what it signified
Student can explain what Mandela means by being the sum of all those African patriots
Student can explain how Mandela's hunger for freedom changed his life
visualIdeas: a web of Mandela's ideas around the word freedom

topics.title: Thinking about Language: Nouns from Verbs
objectives: Student can form nouns from verbs with -(at)ion and -ment, such as govern to government
Student can fill a paragraph with the noun forms of given verbs
visualIdeas: verb-to-noun pairs in two columns

topics.title: Using the Definite Article with Names

topics.title: Idiomatic Expressions
objectives: Student can match idiomatic phrases from the text with their meanings
